actor: TeamPCP (also tracked as PCPcat), per Snyk
impact: Malicious LiteLLM 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 live on PyPI for about three hours; on install the payload harvested cloud, SSH, Git, API and Kubernetes credentials, installed persistence and attempted Kubernetes lateral movement. No confirmed victim organizations; the package sees on the order of millions of downloads per day.
mitigations: Pin LiteLLM to 1.82.6 or earlier and treat any host that installed 1.82.7 or 1.82.8 as compromised and rotate its credentials; audit CI/CD pipelines for unpinned tool versions including GitHub Actions; and check Kubernetes clusters for signs of compromise (Snyk).
name: LiteLLM PyPI package backdoored via a poisoned CI security scanner (TeamPCP)

sources.title: How a Poisoned Security Scanner Became the Key to Backdooring LiteLLM
litellm 1.82.8 Supply Chain Attack on PyPI (March 2026)

summary: On 2026-03-24 two malicious versions of the widely used LiteLLM Python package (1.82.7 and 1.82.8) were published to PyPI and were available for about three hours before PyPI quarantined them. Snyk reports the attackers first compromised the Trivy open-source scanner through its GitHub Action, which LiteLLM's CI pipeline ran without a pinned version, exposing LiteLLM's PyPI publishing credentials; the attackers then used those legitimate credentials to publish releases that passed standard integrity checks. On install the payload harvested cloud, SSH, Git, API and Kubernetes credentials and sent them to an attacker server, installed persistence and attempted to spread to Kubernetes nodes. Snyk attributes the campaign to TeamPCP (also tracked as PCPcat), part of a broader effort that also hit Trivy and Checkmarx KICS. FutureSearch, which discovered the package pulled in as a transitive dependency, confirms the versions and payload. No specific victim organizations are confirmed; LiteLLM is downloaded on the order of millions of times per day.
